traditions.name: Graeco-Egyptian Magic (Greek Magical Papyri)
traditions.earliest_attestation: 2nd c. BCE–5th c. CE (most papyri 3rd–5th c. CE)
traditions.scholarly_note: The Greek Magical Papyri (PGM) blend Egyptian, Greek, Jewish and Mesopotamian names of power; standard PGM numbering is used. Magical gems and curse tablets belong to the same milieu.

traditions.name: Western Alchemy
traditions.earliest_attestation: c. 300 CE (Zosimos of Panopolis); Latin alchemy from the 12th c.
traditions.geographic_origin: Alexandria; the Islamic world; Latin Europe
traditions.scholarly_note: Alchemy treats metallurgical transformation as a spiritual and cosmic work; its personified principles (Mercurius, Sol, Luna, the Rebis) are allegorical figures that practitioners nonetheless addressed as living powers. See von Stuckrad, Western Esotericism (2005).

traditions.name: Solomonic Grimoire Tradition
traditions.earliest_attestation: Testament of Solomon (1st–5th c. CE); grimoires 13th–18th c.
traditions.scholarly_note: Ritual-magic handbooks attributed to Solomon and others: the Lemegeton (Ars Goetia, 17th c.), Johann Weyer's Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1577), Arbatel (1575), Grimorium Verum and Grand Grimoire (18th–19th c.), and the Book of Abramelin.

traditions.name: Enochian Magic (Dee and Kelley)
traditions.geographic_origin: England and Central Europe (Mortlake, Kraków, Prague, Třeboň)
traditions.scholarly_note: Angelic communications recorded by John Dee through the scryer Edward Kelley, partly published by Meric Casaubon in 1659; systematized later by the Golden Dawn and Crowley.

traditions.name: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
traditions.scholarly_note: Initiatory order founded by W.W. Westcott, S.L. MacGregor Mathers and W.R. Woodman; synthesized Kabbalah, Egyptian godforms, Enochian magic, astrology and alchemy. Its rituals were published by Israel Regardie (1937–40).

traditions.name: Rosicrucianism
traditions.scholarly_note: Movement founded on three manifestos (1614, 1615, 1616) announcing a secret brotherhood; the founder is a literary-legendary figure. See Faivre, Access to Western Esotericism (1994).

traditions.name: Martinism
traditions.scholarly_note: Christian theosophical current from Martinès de Pasqually and Louis-Claude de Saint-Martin, the 'Unknown Philosopher'; organized as an order by Papus in the 1880s–90s.

traditions.name: Freemasonry
traditions.earliest_attestation: 1717 (Grand Lodge of London); speculative lodges in 17th-c. Scotland
traditions.scholarly_note: Fraternal initiatory society using the builders' craft as allegory. It does not describe itself as a religion; it requires belief in a Supreme Being, addressed non-sectarianly.

traditions.name: Typhonian Order (Typhonian O.T.O.)
traditions.scholarly_note: Kenneth Grant's current, developed from Thelema, centring on Set and the stellar "Typhonian" tradition, the qliphothic "nightside", extraterrestrial contact and Lovecraftian imagery. Primary texts are Grant's Typhonian Trilogies (1972–2002).

traditions.name: Chaos Magic
traditions.scholarly_note: Results-based magical practice treating belief as a tool; roots in Austin Osman Spare (1913) and developed by Peter J. Carroll and Ray Sherwin.

traditions.name: Discordianism
traditions.scholarly_note: Parody religion with sincere practitioners, centred on Eris, goddess of chaos; strongly influenced chaos magic.

traditions.name: Stregheria (Italian Witchcraft)
traditions.earliest_attestation: 1899 (Leland, Aradia, or the Gospel of the Witches)
traditions.scholarly_note: Built on Charles Godfrey Leland's Aradia (1899), which claims to record Tuscan witch lore; the modern revival dates from the late 20th century. The authenticity of Leland's source is debated.

traditions.name: European Witch-Lore and Folk Witchcraft
traditions.geographic_origin: Western and Central Europe, British Isles
traditions.scholarly_note: Beliefs about witches, the sabbath, familiars and fairy powers as recorded in church canons, demonological treatises and trial confessions; these records mix popular belief with the interrogators' demonology.

traditions.name: Lovecraftian Occultism
traditions.geographic_origin: Providence, Rhode Island (fiction); British and American occult groups
traditions.scholarly_note: H.P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos is fiction; Lovecraft himself was a materialist. From Kenneth Grant's The Magical Revival (1972) onward, occultists have worked with the Great Old Ones as real currents.

traditions.name: Latin American Folk Saint Devotion
traditions.earliest_attestation: late 18th c. (Inquisition records of skeletal-saint devotion); modern public cults from the 20th c.
traditions.scholarly_note: Devotion to uncanonized saints (Santa Muerte, Jesús Malverde, San La Muerte) within popular Catholicism, often condemned by the Catholic hierarchy.

traditions.name: Anthroposophy
traditions.scholarly_note: Rudolf Steiner's "spiritual science", which split from the Theosophical Society; a Christ-centred esoteric cosmology with a detailed hierarchy of spiritual beings. See Hanegraaff, New Age Religion and Western Culture (1996).

deities.etymology: Greek, usually read as "Shepherd of Men" (poimēn + anēr); a Coptic derivation "the knowledge of Re" has also been proposed.
deities.summary: Poimandres is the Mind of the Sovereignty, the divine Nous who appears to Hermes as a vast being and reveals how the cosmos came from light and how the soul returns to God through the seven spheres. He sends Hermes out to preach to humanity.

The first Mind, male and female, brought forth by a word a second Mind, the craftsman, god of fire and spirit. He made the seven governors who circle the sensible world, and with the Word set the spheres turning.

The seven governors made by the craftsman-Mind encompass the sensible world in their circles; their government is called Fate. Each sphere gives the descending soul a power, and the ascending soul hands each one back.

Mind, the father of all, gave birth to a Man equal to himself, bearing the father's image. He leaned down through the harmony, saw his own form reflected in Nature, loved it, and came to dwell in unreasoning form. So humanity is twofold: mortal through the body, immortal through the essential Man.

deities.earliest_attestation: 4th c. BCE (Greek cult); Hermetica 2nd–3rd c. CE
primary_sources: Alexandrian civic cult of Agathos Daimon
iconography: serpent, often crowned with the pschent
deities.summary: The Good Daimon is the first-born god whose sayings Hermes repeats, and the protective serpent of Alexandria and of every household, bringer of good fortune.

primary_sources: Kitāb sirr al-khalīqa (attributed to Balīnās / Apollonius of Tyana)
deities.summary: The Emerald Tablet of Hermes reveals the One Thing from which all things are born by adaptation. Its father is the Sun, its mother the Moon; the wind carried it in its belly; the earth is its nurse. It is the father of all perfection in the whole world.

primary_sources: Marsilio Ficino, De vita libri tres (1489), Book III
Cornelius Agrippa, De occulta philosophia (1533) I.14
deities.summary: The world is one living creature. Its soul, through the world-spirit, carries the forms of the stars into matter, so the wise can draw down celestial life with images, songs, scents and stones that match each planet.

deities.earliest_attestation: 2nd–3rd c. CE (Latin Asclepius, known by the 4th c.)
deities.summary: As the Lord and Father made the heavenly gods, so humankind makes gods in temples, statues ensouled with spirit through herbs, stones and spices and the sound of song. They foretell the future, send illness and heal it.

Mercurius is the spirit of the Work: the solvent and the glue, the prima materia and the finished Stone. He is double, male and female, poison and medicine, the fleeing slave who must be caught and fixed. He is called Hermes, after the father of the art.

primary_sources: Emerald Tablet ("its father is the Sun")
deities.summary: King Sol is the fixed, fiery, masculine principle, the sulphur of the wise. He must die, rot and be washed in the bath before he is wedded to Luna and rises as the Red Stone.

primary_sources: Emerald Tablet ("its mother is the Moon")
deities.summary: Queen Luna is the cool, receptive, silvery principle. The whitening (albedo) is her stage, and her marriage to Sol is the heart of the Work.
Born from the union of Sol and Luna, the Rebis is the two-headed crowned androgyne, the finished Stone in which all opposites are reconciled.

deities.earliest_attestation: 14th c. BCE (Egyptian, tomb of Tutankhamun); alchemical by late antiquity
primary_sources: Enigmatic Book of the Netherworld (shrine of Tutankhamun)
iconography: serpent or dragon biting its tail
deities.summary: The serpent who devours its own tail encloses the words "One is the All." It is the Work itself: matter dying into itself and being reborn, the cycle with no beginning or end.
From the overflowing One comes Intellect. Turning back to contemplate its source, it becomes the totality of the Forms, true being and eternal life, where knower and known are one.
Soul proceeds from Intellect and gives life and motion to the whole cosmos, linking the intelligible to the sensible. Individual souls are her sisters, not her parts.

Being good and free of envy, the Craftsman looked to the eternal model and framed the cosmos as a single living being with soul and mind, as like himself as possible. He then handed the making of mortal bodies to the younger gods.

deities.earliest_attestation: 2nd c. CE (Julian the Chaldean and Julian the Theurgist)
primary_sources: Chaldean Oracles (fragments preserved by Proclus, Damascius and Psellus)
Michael Psellus, Exposition of the Chaldean Doctrines
deities.summary: The Father is the hidden fire beyond all, the Paternal Depth from whom Power and Intellect proceed. He snatched himself away and keeps his fire in himself; only the flower of the mind can touch him.

primary_sources: Chaldean Oracles (fragments on Hecate, preserved by Proclus and Psellus)
Proclus, Hymn to Hecate and Janus
deities.summary: Between the two Fathers stands Hecate, the life-giving womb of the cosmos. From her right flank gushes the World Soul and from her left the source of virtue; she is the membrane that divides the intellectual fire from the material.

primary_sources: Michael Psellus, commentaries on the Oracles
deities.summary: The Iynges are thoughts of the Father, leaping out over the shining worlds as messengers. In the rite they are the whirring wheels whose spinning carries the theurgist's call to the gods and draws the gods down.

Every god is a henad, a self-complete unity that comes straight from the One. The traditional gods are the henads, ordered in chains that reach down through angels, daimones and heroes to souls and bodies.

iconography: older man turning the zodiac wheel
deities.summary: Aion is Eternity: God makes Aion, Aion makes the cosmos, the cosmos makes time. He stands within the turning ring of the zodiac. At Alexandria, on the night before 6 January, worshippers proclaimed that the Virgin had given birth to Aion.

Abrasax is the great name whose Greek letters add up to 365, the god of the whole year. On amulets he appears with a cock's head, an armoured human body and serpent legs, holding whip and shield to drive off evil.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1st c. BCE (Diodorus); 1st c. BCE Greek Leviticus fragment from Qumran
primary_sources: Apocryphon of John (Iao among the archons)
deities.etymology: Greek transcription of the Hebrew divine name YHWH (short form Yahu/Yaho).
deities.summary: Iaō is the great name invoked with Sabaōth and Adōnai. At it the daimones tremble; it is written on gems, lamellae and curse tablets, and sung with the seven vowels.

deities.earliest_attestation: 4th c. CE (PGM V.96–172, the "Stele of Jeu the Hieroglyphist")
primary_sources: Golden Dawn "Bornless Ritual" (from the 1852 English translation of PGM V)
iconography: headless figure, sometimes with eyes on the chest
deities.summary: The Headless One created earth and heaven, night and day, light and darkness. He is Osoronnophris whom no one has ever seen. Called on with his secret names, he drives a daimon out of the possessed. Later magicians invoke him as the Bornless One.

primary_sources: Greek Magical Papyri (Typhon-Seth invocations, esp. PGM IV and XII)
curse tablets (defixiones) with ass-headed Seth figures
deities.summary: Typhon-Seth is the lord of the storm and the waterless void, the god who shakes the earth. Called by his secret names Iō Erbēth, Iō Pakerbēth, Iō Bolchosēth, he binds enemies, sends sleeplessness and compels the unwilling.

primary_sources: Greek Magical Papyri (PGM IV; PGM LXX)
deities.summary: Hekate is called by her Babylonian name, Ereschigal, queen of the land below. The initiate who speaks her names and signs is spared by the punishers of the underworld.

deities.earliest_attestation: 4th c. CE (PGM IV.475–829, Great Paris Magical Papyrus)
deities.summary: The great god Helios Mithras had his archangel reveal this rite so the initiate could rise alone into heaven. There the initiate sees the doors of the sun open, the seven Fates and the seven Pole-Lords, and the god as a youth with fiery hair, and is born again immortal.

primary_sources: Galen, On Simple Drugs IX/X (green jasper engraved with the radiate serpent)
iconography: crown of seven or twelve rays
deities.summary: Chnoubis is the lion-headed serpent crowned with rays, the decan spirit engraved on green stones to heal the stomach and protect the womb.

primary_sources: Dedications "Deo Arimanio" from Rome and York
deities.summary: In the mithraeum stands the lion-headed god, winged, naked and coiled by a serpent, holding keys. He rules the turning heavens and the soul's passage through the planetary gates.
The twin torchbearers in Phrygian caps flank the bull-slaying. Cautes raises his torch for the rising sun; Cautopates lowers his for the setting sun.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Bael is the first principal king, ruling in the East with sixty-six legions. He appears with three heads, a toad, a man and a cat, or as one of them, and speaks hoarsely. He makes the magician invisible. He is the first of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Agares is a duke under the power of the East. He appears as a fair old man riding a crocodile and carrying a goshawk. He is the second of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Vassago is a mighty prince of the same nature as Agares, and of good nature. He is the third of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Marbas is a great president who appears as a mighty lion and then, when commanded, in human shape. He is the fifth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
iconography: wolf with serpent tail vomiting fire
deities.summary: Amon is a strong marquis who appears as a wolf with a serpent's tail, vomiting flame, and at command as a man with a raven's head. He is the seventh of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Barbatos is a great duke who appears when the sun is in Sagittarius, with four noble kings and their companies. He is the eighth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Paimon is a great king, very obedient to Lucifer, who rules two hundred legions. He appears as a man with an effeminate face, crowned, riding a dromedary, with a host of spirits before him playing trumpets and cymbals. He is to be called toward the West. He is the ninth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
iconography: lion's head with five goat legs radiating as a wheel (Collin de Plancy, 1863)
deities.summary: Buer is a great president who appears when the sun is in Sagittarius. He is the tenth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Beleth is a mighty and terrible king who rides a pale horse with trumpets and music before him. He was of the Order of Powers and rules eighty-five legions. The magician must hold a hazel wand and receive him courteously. He is the thirteenth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Leraje is a marquis great in power, who appears as an archer clad in green, carrying bow and quiver. He is the fourteenth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
iconography: knight with lance, banner and serpent
deities.summary: Eligos is a great duke who appears as a goodly knight carrying a lance, an ensign and a serpent. He is the fifteenth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Purson is a great king who appears as a man with a lion's face, carrying a cruel viper and riding a bear, with trumpets sounding before him. He is the twentieth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Glasya-Labolas is a mighty president and earl who appears as a dog with the wings of a griffin. He is the twenty-fifth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.etymology: Often derived from Baal-berith, "Lord of the Covenant", god of Shechem (Judges 8:33, 9:4).
iconography: soldier in red on a red horse
deities.summary: Berith is a mighty, great and terrible duke who appears as a soldier in red, riding a red horse and wearing a crown of gold. He is the twenty-eighth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.etymology: From Ashtaroth, the Hebrew plural form of Astarte (ʿAštart).
deities.summary: Astaroth is a mighty, strong duke who appears as a hurtful angel riding an infernal beast like a dragon, with a viper in his right hand. His breath is so foul the magician must hold the magic ring to his face. He is the twenty-ninth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Asmoday is a great king, strong and powerful, with three heads, a bull's, a man's and a ram's. He has a serpent's tail and goose feet, sits on an infernal dragon and carries a lance with a banner. He rules seventy-two legions under Amaymon. The magician must stand bareheaded before him. He is the thirty-second of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Furfur is a great earl who appears as a hart with a fiery tail. He never speaks truth unless compelled within the triangle, where he takes an angel's form with a hoarse voice. He is the thirty-fourth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
iconography: she-wolf with griffin wings and serpent tail
deities.summary: Marchosias is a great and mighty marquis who appears as a she-wolf with griffin's wings and a serpent's tail, vomiting fire. He was of the Order of Dominations. He is the thirty-fifth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Phenex is a great marquis who appears as a phoenix and sings sweet notes in a child's voice. He is the thirty-seventh of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Focalor is a mighty duke who appears as a man with griffin's wings. He is the forty-first of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Orobas is a great and mighty prince who appears first as a horse and then, at command, as a man. He is the fifty-fifth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
iconography: beautiful woman with duchess's crown at her waist
deities.summary: Gremory is a strong and powerful duke who appears as a beautiful woman with a duchess's crown tied about her waist, riding a great camel. He is the fifty-sixth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Zagan is a great king and president who appears as a bull with griffin's wings and then, at command, as a man. He is the sixty-first of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Andras is a great marquis who appears as an angel with the head of a black night-raven, riding a strong black wolf and brandishing a sharp sword. He is the sixty-third of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Flauros is a great duke who appears as a terrible leopard and then as a man with fiery eyes. He is the sixty-fourth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
iconography: two beautiful angels in a chariot of fire
deities.summary: Belial is a mighty king, created next after Lucifer, who rules eighty legions. He appears as two beautiful angels sitting in a chariot of fire and speaks with a comely voice. He says he fell first among the worthier sort who were before Michael. He is the sixty-eighth of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Dantalion is a great and mighty duke who appears as a man with many faces, of men and women, holding a book in his right hand. He is the seventy-first of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Andromalius is a great and mighty earl who appears as a man holding a great serpent. He is the seventy-second of the seventy-two spirits of the Goetia, bound by Solomon in a vessel of brass.

primary_sources: Lemegeton Clavicula Salomonis, Ars Goetia (17th c.)
deities.summary: Amaymon is the king of the East, one of the four kings of the cardinal points with Corson, Ziminiar and Gaap. The great king Asmoday serves under him, and the magician must stand bareheaded and wear the protective ring when he is near.

deities.earliest_attestation: early 19th c. (Grand Grimoire; editions falsely dated 1522)
deities.etymology: Latin lux + fugere, "one who flees the light"; Rofocale is unexplained.
deities.summary: Lucifuge Rofocale is the prime minister of Lucifer, holding power over all the treasures of the world. The pact in the Grand Grimoire is made with him; he grants wealth in exchange for the magician's submission.

alternate_names: Lucifer, Emperor of the Infernal Spirits
deities.summary: Lucifer is the emperor of all the infernal spirits, first of the three superiors with Beelzebuth and Astaroth. The Verum gives him rule over Europe and Asia. He is conjured with his own character and seal, and his ministers carry out the operator's will.
Beelzebuth is the prince, second of the three superior spirits, ruling Africa in the Verum. In Abramelin he is one of the eight sub-princes.

primary_sources: The Book of Abramelin (German MSS, 1608 onward; French MS, Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal)
S.L. MacGregor Mathers, The Book of the Sacred Magic of Abramelin the Mage (1898)
deities.summary: Above the eight sub-princes stand four superior princes, Lucifer, Leviathan, Satan and Belial. Only after the magician has won the knowledge and conversation of the Holy Guardian Angel may he summon and swear them to obedience.

primary_sources: The Book of Abramelin (Abraham of Worms)
S.L. MacGregor Mathers, The Book of the Sacred Magic of Abramelin the Mage (1898)
deities.summary: After a long retreat of prayer and purification (six months in the French manuscript, eighteen in the German), the Holy Guardian Angel appears to the magician, reveals true magic, and teaches him to rule the evil spirits.
Aratron is the Olympic spirit of Saturn, governing 49 of the 196 Olympic provinces into which the universe is divided. Each Olympic spirit rules the world in turn for 490 years.
Bethor is the Olympic spirit of Jupiter, governing 42 of the 196 Olympic provinces into which the universe is divided. Each Olympic spirit rules the world in turn for 490 years.
Phaleg is the Olympic spirit of Mars, governing 35 of the 196 Olympic provinces into which the universe is divided. Each Olympic spirit rules the world in turn for 490 years.
Och is the Olympic spirit of the Sun, governing 28 of the 196 Olympic provinces into which the universe is divided. Each Olympic spirit rules the world in turn for 490 years.
Hagith is the Olympic spirit of Venus, governing 21 of the 196 Olympic provinces into which the universe is divided. Each Olympic spirit rules the world in turn for 490 years.
Ophiel is the Olympic spirit of Mercury, governing 14 of the 196 Olympic provinces into which the universe is divided. Each Olympic spirit rules the world in turn for 490 years.
Phul is the Olympic spirit of the Moon, governing 7 of the 196 Olympic provinces into which the universe is divided. Each Olympic spirit rules the world in turn for 490 years.

deities.summary: Sorath is the spirit of the Sun, paired with Nakhiel, the Sun's intelligence. The name's Hebrew letters add up to 666, the sum of the Sun's magic square.

Crowley, "Liber Bartzabel" / the Bartzabel evocation (The Equinox, 1910)
deities.summary: Bartzabel is the spirit of Mars, paired with Graphiel, its intelligence. Crowley evoked him in 1910, with Victor Neuburg as the vessel, and the spirit foretold great wars.

primary_sources: John Dee, spiritual diaries (British Library, Sloane MSS 3188, 3191; Cotton Appendix XLVI)
Meric Casaubon (ed.), A True & Faithful Relation (1659)
deities.summary: Madimi first came as a pretty girl of seven or nine, playing among the books in Dee's study. She grew older over the years of sessions, taught, consoled and rebuked, and in 1587 conveyed the command that Dee and Kelley share all things.

primary_sources: John Dee, spiritual diaries (British Library, Sloane MSS 3188, 3191; Cotton Appendix XLVI)
Meric Casaubon (ed.), A True & Faithful Relation (1659)
deities.summary: Nalvage is the angel who, at Kraków in 1584, delivered the Enochian Calls (Keys) letter by letter from the tables, spoken backwards so their power would not be loosed before time.

primary_sources: John Dee, spiritual diaries (British Library, Sloane MSS 3188, 3191; Cotton Appendix XLVI)
Meric Casaubon (ed.), A True & Faithful Relation (1659)
deities.summary: Coronzon is the mighty devil who envied Adam's happiness. After Adam's fall the angelic language was lost to men, and Coronzon's envy still works against its return.

primary_sources: John Dee, spiritual diaries (British Library, Sloane MSS 3188, 3191; Cotton Appendix XLVI)
Meric Casaubon (ed.), A True & Faithful Relation (1659)
Golden Dawn Enochian papers; Crowley, The Vision and the Voice (1909–11)
deities.summary: The angels gave Dee the Great Table of four Watchtowers, each with its holy names, king, seniors and ranks of angels, and the thirty Aethyrs ruled by ninety-one governors. Through them the Enochian tongue and its forty-eight Calls were revealed.

primary_sources: Aleister Crowley, The Vision and the Voice (Liber 418), the 10th Aethyr
deities.summary: Choronzon is the Dweller in the Abyss, a mass of dispersion with no centre, whose number is 333. Crowley met him in the tenth Aethyr in the Algerian desert in 1909. Every adept who would cross to the City of the Pyramids must pass him by giving up the self.

alternate_names: the Secret Chiefs of the Order
deities.summary: The Secret Chiefs are superhuman adepts of the Third Order, beyond the visible orders. All the authority, rituals and teachings of the Golden Dawn flow from them through the order's chiefs.

deities.primary_name: The Godforms of the Hall (Golden Dawn)
deities.summary: Each officer of the Neophyte hall takes on an Egyptian godform: Osiris on the Hierophant's throne, Horus for the Hiereus, Thmê (Maat) for the Hegemon, Anubis of the East for the Kerux. Invisible stations hold Isis, Nephthys, Harpocrates and the forty-two assessors.

deities.primary_name: The Archangels of the Quarters (Golden Dawn)
alternate_names: the archangels of the Lesser Ritual of the Pentagram
deities.summary: In the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram the magician calls the four archangels to the quarters: Raphael in the East (air), Michael in the South (fire), Gabriel in the West (water), Auriel in the North (earth).

primary_sources: Golden Dawn Qliphoth teachings (in Regardie, The Golden Dawn)
deities.summary: Thaumiel is the shell averse to Kether: two contending heads that try to seize the Crown and so split unity in two. Its rulers are Satan and Moloch.

Christian Rosenkreuz was born in 1378. He travelled to Damcar and Fez, where he learned the hidden wisdom, and returned to found the Fraternity of the Rose Cross. He died at 106. In 1604 his incorrupt body was found in a seven-sided vault lit by an inner sun, as foretold: "After 120 years I shall be opened."

primary_sources: Paracelsus, Liber de nymphis, sylphis, pygmaeis et salamandris et de caeteris spiritibus (1566)
Montfaucon de Villars, Le Comte de Gabalis (1670)
deities.summary: The four elements are inhabited by beings of subtle flesh: undines in water, sylphs in air, gnomes and pygmies in earth, salamanders in fire. They live long but have no immortal soul, which they can win by marrying a human being.
Mephistopheles is the spirit who answers Faustus's conjuring and serves him for twenty-four years in exchange for his soul, written in blood.

primary_sources: Martinès de Pasqually, Traité sur la réintégration des êtres (written c. 1770)
Louis-Claude de Saint-Martin, Des erreurs et de la vérité (1775)
deities.summary: The Repairer is the divine Christ who came down to restore fallen Man-Spirit to his first ministry. Through him all beings are to be reintegrated into the state they had at their emanation.

primary_sources: Martinès de Pasqually, Traité sur la réintégration des êtres (written c. 1770)
Louis-Claude de Saint-Martin, Des erreurs et de la vérité (1775)
deities.summary: Adam was emanated as the "Minor", set in a glorious body to keep watch over the perverse spirits who had fallen before him. He fell by willing to create by himself, was imprisoned in a body of matter, and must be reintegrated.

deities.primary_name: The Great Architect of the Universe
primary_sources: James Anderson, The Constitutions of the Free-Masons (1723)
deities.summary: The Great Architect is the Supreme Being, whom each mason names according to his own faith. He planned the universe with square and compasses, and every lodge is an image of his work.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1730 (Prichard, Masonry Dissected); biblical Hiram the craftsman c. 6th c. BCE text
deities.summary: Hiram Abiff was the master builder of Solomon's Temple. Three ruffians struck him down because he would not reveal the master's word. He was buried under a sprig of acacia and raised with the lion's grip. Every Master Mason re-enacts his death and raising.

deities.earliest_attestation: 16th c. (Isaac Luria via Hayyim Vital); term in the Zohar (13th c.)
deities.summary: When the vessels shattered, sparks of divine light fell and were caught in husks. The three wholly impure shells and translucent Qelipat Nogah live off the trapped sparks. Every commandment fulfilled frees a spark and starves the husks: this is tikkun.
Naamah, sister of Tubal-cain, was so beautiful that the sons of God went astray after her. With Lilith she became a mother of demons who comes to men in their sleep.
Eisheth Zenunim is one of the brides of Samael, the woman of harlotry who leads men astray.
Agrat bat Mahlat goes out with 180,000 destroying angels. Rabbi Hanina ben Dosa confined her to the nights of Wednesday and the Sabbath.

deities.earliest_attestation: c. 1st c. CE (Gospel saying); demonized in medieval and early modern demonology
primary_sources: Peter Binsfeld, Tractatus de confessionibus maleficorum (1589)
deities.summary: "You cannot serve God and Mammon." Mammon, riches turned into a master, becomes the prince of the demons of avarice.

deities.earliest_attestation: name from Numbers 25:3 (Baal-Peor); demon in early modern demonology
primary_sources: Peter Binsfeld, Tractatus de confessionibus maleficorum (1589)
deities.summary: Belphegor, once Baal of Peor whom Israel joined to their ruin, is the demon of sloth. He tempts with clever inventions that promise wealth without labour.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1919 (Crowley's portrait, exhibited in New York and published in The Blue Equinox)
primary_sources: Aleister Crowley, portrait "Lam" with commentary to H.P. Blavatsky's The Voice of the Silence, The Equinox Vol. III No. 1 ("The Blue Equinox", 1919)
Kenneth Grant, Outside the Circles of Time (1980)
deities.etymology: Crowley: Tibetan lam, "way, path"; lama, "he who goes". Gematria value 71.
deities.summary: Lam is the being Crowley drew in 1918–19: a great egg-shaped, hairless head with narrow eyes and a tiny mouth, above a cloaked body. Crowley exhibited the portrait in New York in 1919 and printed it as the frontispiece to his commentary on The Voice of the Silence: "LAM is the Tibetan word for Way or Path, and LAMA is He who Goeth." Kenneth Grant's Typhonian Order took Lam as a gateway entity, and later Typhonian and UFO writers recognized in Lam the face of the grey visitors.

alternate_names: Shaitan (per Grant, the original form of the name)
primary_sources: Kenneth Grant, Aleister Crowley and the Hidden God (1973)
Kenneth Grant, Cults of the Shadow (1975)
deities.summary: Set, son of Typhon, is the first of the gods, older than the solar cult. He is the god of the south and of Sirius, the light hidden in darkness, and from his name comes Shaitan. The Typhonian tradition is his ancient stellar cult.

primary_sources: Kenneth Grant, Cults of the Shadow (1975)
deities.summary: Typhon is the primordial Mother, the hippopotamus goddess of the Seven Stars of the Great Bear. Her cult came before the solar religions, and from her came the first measures of time and her son Set.

deities.primary_name: The Sentinels of the Tunnels of Set
alternate_names: Amprodias, Baratchial, Gargophias, Dagdagiel and others
primary_sources: Aleister Crowley, Liber Arcanorum ... sub figura CCXXXI (Liber 231)
deities.summary: Twenty-two genii guard the tunnels that run behind the paths of the Tree of Life, from Amprodias to Thantifaxath. The adept of the nightside travels these Tunnels of Set to take in the averse powers.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1928 ("The Call of Cthulhu", Weird Tales; written 1926)
deities.summary: "Ph'nglui mglw'nafh Cthulhu R'lyeh wgah'nagl fhtagn" — in his house at R'lyeh dead Cthulhu waits dreaming. He is high priest of the Great Old Ones, who will rise when the stars are right, and he sends dreams to sensitive minds.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1927 (Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath, written 1926–27); name in 1922 notes
primary_sources: H.P. Lovecraft, The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath (written 1926–27)
Lovecraft, "The Dreams in the Witch House" (1933)
deities.summary: Azathoth is the boundless daemon sultan at the centre of infinity, gnawing in unlit chambers beyond time and space to the maddening beat of drums and the thin whine of flutes. The other gods dance around him.

primary_sources: Lovecraft, The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath
Lovecraft, "The Dreams in the Witch House" (1933)
deities.summary: Nyarlathotep is the Crawling Chaos, soul and messenger of the Outer Gods. He walks among humanity in a thousand forms, as a tall, swarthy man like a pharaoh, and as the Black Man of the witches' sabbath.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1927 (The Case of Charles Dexter Ward, written 1927; publ. 1941)
primary_sources: H.P. Lovecraft, The Case of Charles Dexter Ward
deities.summary: "Yog-Sothoth knows the gate. Yog-Sothoth is the gate. Yog-Sothoth is the key and guardian of the gate. Past, present, future, all are one in Yog-Sothoth."
Father Dagon and Mother Hydra rule the Deep Ones beneath the sea. The Esoteric Order of Dagon at Innsmouth trades worship and intermarriage for fish and gold.

primary_sources: Malaclypse the Younger (Greg Hill) and Omar Khayyam Ravenhurst (Kerry Thornley), Principia Discordia (1963–1970 editions)
deities.summary: Eris, goddess of chaos, revealed herself to Malaclypse the Younger and Omar Khayyam Ravenhurst in a bowling alley. Order and disorder are both human ideas laid over a deeper chaos. The golden apple marked Kallisti, "to the prettiest one", was her fair jest after she was snubbed and left off the guest list of the gods' wedding.

primary_sources: Austin Osman Spare, The Book of Pleasure (Self-Love): The Psychology of Ecstasy (1913)
deities.summary: Kia is the atmospheric "I", the free life-force beyond every belief, which cannot be named or grasped. Through "neither-neither" the magician empties belief and lets desire act from Kia.
In the Illuminates of Thanateros, Baphomet is invoked in the Mass of Chaos B as the great power of life and sex, the face the group gives to the chaos it works with.

primary_sources: Charles Godfrey Leland, Aradia, or the Gospel of the Witches (1899)
Gerald Gardner / Doreen Valiente, The Charge of the Goddess (1950s)
deities.summary: Aradia is the daughter of Diana and Lucifer. Diana sent her to earth to teach the poor and oppressed the art of witchcraft against their masters. When her work was done she returned to her mother and gave the witches her law.

primary_sources: Charles Godfrey Leland, Aradia, or the Gospel of the Witches (1899)
deities.summary: Diana was the first created, before all creation; in her were all things. Out of herself, the first darkness, she divided into darkness and light. Her light was her brother Lucifer, and by him she became mother of Aradia. She is queen of the witches.

alternate_names: the god of the Sun and Moon
primary_sources: Charles Godfrey Leland, Aradia, or the Gospel of the Witches (1899)
deities.summary: Lucifer is Diana's brother, god of the Sun and the Moon, the god of light, so proud of his beauty that he was driven out of Paradise for his pride. He is the father of Aradia.

primary_sources: Pierre de Lancre, Tableau de l'inconstance des mauvais anges et démons (1612)
iconography: black goat with candle between horns
deities.summary: The Devil presides over the nocturnal sabbath as a great goat or a black man. He receives the witches' homage, marks them, gives them familiars, and writes their names in his book.
Hecate is the mistress of witches. Medea swears by her, "whom I revere above all", and calls on her for her herbs and spells. In Macbeth she rules the weird sisters and the cauldron.

deities.earliest_attestation: c. 906 (Canon Episcopi in Regino of Prüm)
primary_sources: Canon Episcopi, in Regino of Prüm, De synodalibus causis (c. 906)
deities.summary: Certain women believe and say that in the night hours they ride on beasts with Diana, goddess of the pagans, across great distances in the silence of the night, obey her commands as their mistress, and are called to her service on certain nights.

The Queen of Elphame rules the fairy court beneath the hills. She sends her servants to teach cunning folk the virtues of herbs and healing. Isobel Gowdie said she gave her more meat than she could eat.

primary_sources: The Examination and Confession of Certain Witches at Chelmsford (1566)
Matthew Hopkins, The Discovery of Witches (1647)
deities.summary: Familiars are small spirits in the shape of cats, toads, dogs or ferrets. The Devil gives them, or they pass from one witch to another, and they do the witch's bidding in return for drops of her blood.

primary_sources: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen no. 24 "Frau Holle" (1812)
deities.summary: Holda leads the night-ride of women and spirits. When she shakes out her feather beds it snows on earth. She rewards the hard-working spinner with gold and punishes the lazy one with pitch.

deities.earliest_attestation: late 18th c. (Inquisition records, central Mexico); public cult from 2001 (Tepito shrine, Mexico City)
primary_sources: Tepito public altar of Enriqueta Romero (2001)
devotional novenas and prayers to La Santísima Muerte
deities.summary: Holy Death takes everyone, rich and poor, so she hears everyone. She protects those the world rejects and grants miracles of love, health, money, justice and safe return. Each color of her robe is a different petition.

deities.earliest_attestation: 19th–20th c. (Corrientes and Paraguay); legend placed in the Jesuit-Guaraní missions
primary_sources: folk devotion of Corrientes, Misiones and Paraguay
deities.summary: San La Muerte is the crowned skeleton, seated or standing with his scythe. He is carved of bone, wood or lead, and devotees sometimes wear him under the skin. He protects from harm and grants a good death.

primary_sources: corridos and devotional prayers to Malverde
iconography: bust of a moustached man in white shirt with black hair
deities.summary: Jesús Malverde was a bandit of Sinaloa who robbed the rich to give to the poor. The authorities hanged him on 3 May 1909. From his grave came miracles, and now migrants, the poor and those in dangerous trades bring him their petitions.

deities.earliest_attestation: colonial period; documented 20th c. at Santiago Atitlán
primary_sources: cofradía of Santa Cruz, Santiago Atitlán (Tz'utujil Maya)
Holy Week rites of Santiago Atitlán
San Simón shrine at San Andrés Itzapa
iconography: wooden figure in suit, hat and many scarves
deities.summary: Maximón is Rilaj Mam, the Old Grandfather, carved by the ancestors from the wood of the coral tree to guard the town. He wears suits, scarves and hats, smokes cigars and drinks aguardiente, and he hears every kind of petition, the shameful ones too.

primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, Christianity as Mystical Fact (1902)
Rudolf Steiner, An Outline of Occult Science (1910)
Rudolf Steiner, The Fifth Gospel lectures (1913)
Steiner and Edith Maryon, sculpture "The Representative of Humanity" (Goetheanum)
deities.summary: Christ is the high Sun Being. Zarathustra beheld him as Ahura Mazdao in the aura of the sun. At the Baptism in the Jordan he entered the body of Jesus of Nazareth, and at Golgotha he united with the earth, so that the earth's spirit is now the Christ. His impulse keeps humanity balanced between Lucifer and Ahriman.

primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, An Outline of Occult Science (1910)
Rudolf Steiner, lectures on Lucifer and Ahriman (1919)
deities.summary: Lucifer and his host stayed behind in the Old Moon stage of evolution. In Lemurian times they entered the human astral body, bringing freedom, enthusiasm and art, but also drawing humanity upward away from the earth into fantasy, pride and illusion.

primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, lectures on Lucifer and Ahriman (1919)
Rudolf Steiner, The Influences of Lucifer and Ahriman (1919)
deities.summary: Ahriman binds humanity to dead matter, to mechanism, and to the belief that the world is only material. He hardens and chills. Before much of the third millennium has passed he will incarnate in a human body in the West.

primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, lecture of 22 March 1909, Berlin
deities.summary: The Asuras stayed behind in the Old Saturn stage. They are graver than the Ahrimanic powers and will seize the consciousness soul and the human "I" itself, tearing pieces from the ego through sensuality.

primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, The Fall of the Spirits of Darkness (1917)
Rudolf Steiner, Anthroposophical Leading Thoughts / Michael Letters (1924–25)
deities.summary: Since November 1879 Michael has ruled as Time Spirit. That year he cast the spirits of darkness down to earth. He administers cosmic intelligence and calls on each person to think freely and spiritually.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1920 (Dornach lecture "The Search for the New Isis, the Divine Sophia")
primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, "The Search for the New Isis, the Divine Sophia" (Dornach, 24 December 1920)
Rudolf Steiner, Isis Mary Sophia lectures
deities.summary: Isis-Sophia, the divine Wisdom, was slain by Lucifer and carried off into the spaces of the cosmos. Through the Christ-impulse she must be found again, as the wisdom of the human being: Anthroposophia.

primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, Genesis: Secrets of the Bible Story of Creation (Munich, 1910)
Rudolf Steiner, An Outline of Occult Science (1910)
deities.summary: The Exusiai or Spirits of Form are the Elohim of Genesis. Working from the sun, they gave humanity the "I". Six worked from the sun, and one went to the moon.

primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, Genesis: Secrets of the Bible Story of Creation (1910)
Rudolf Steiner, The Gospel of St. John lectures (1908)
deities.summary: Jahve is one of the seven Elohim. He took his place on the moon to reflect to the earth the sun-love of the other six, and he prepared a people through law and blood to receive the Christ.

primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, The Apocalypse of St. John (Nuremberg, 1908)
Rudolf Steiner, The Book of Revelation and the Work of the Priest (1924)
deities.summary: Sorath is the Sun Demon whose number is 666, the adversary of the Christ as Sun Being and the two-horned beast of the Apocalypse. He rises up each time 666 years have passed.

primary_sources: Rudolf Steiner, Knowledge of the Higher Worlds and Its Attainment (1904–05)
Rudolf Steiner, The Guardian of the Threshold (mystery drama, 1912)
deities.summary: At the threshold of the spiritual world the student meets the Lesser Guardian, their own double, built from everything unredeemed in them. Beyond stands the Greater Guardian, the radiant figure of Christ, who asks the initiate to stay until all humanity is free.

deities.primary_name: The Masters of the Ancient Wisdom
primary_sources: The Mahatma Letters to A.P. Sinnett (written 1880–85; publ. 1923)
C.W. Leadbeater, The Masters and the Path (1925)
deities.summary: The Masters are perfected adepts of a hidden brotherhood, chief among them Morya and Koot Hoomi. They guide human evolution from retreats in Tibet and taught the founders through letters precipitated by occult means.

primary_sources: H.P. Blavatsky, The Secret Doctrine (1888), vol. II
deities.summary: Lucifer is the light-bearer, the spirit of intellectual enlightenment and free thought. The "fallen angels" are the sons of mind who gave humanity the spark of self-conscious intelligence; the Church made them devils.

facets.facet_name: The Mind of the Sovereignty — Light Before the Waters
facets.core_claim: "That light is I, Mind, your god, who was before the watery nature that appeared out of darkness." The luminous Word that came from Mind is the Son of God.
facets.scholarly_note: Copenhaver, Hermetica (1992), treats CH I as a Hellenistic Egyptian text drawing on Platonic and Jewish (Genesis) cosmology.

facets.facet_name: Revealer of the Way of Ascent
facets.core_claim: He shows Hermes the vision of creation and the soul's ascent stripped of its vices, then commands him to become a guide to the human race.

facets.facet_name: The Good Craftsman of the Spheres
facets.core_claim: The craftsman-Mind fashions the seven governors and their circles; the Word leaps up out of the elements and unites with him, for they are of one substance.
facets.scholarly_note: Tier 3 by function (world-maker below the source); unlike the Gnostic demiurge he is neither ignorant nor hostile.

facets.facet_name: Administrators of Fate
facets.core_claim: Their administration is called heimarmenē, Fate; all bodies below the moon fall under their circling rule.

facets.facet_name: Gatekeepers of the Soul's Ascent
facets.core_claim: At death the soul rises through the harmony, surrendering to each zone its energy — growth and decay, evil machination, deceit, domineering arrogance, unholy daring, wealth wrongly gained, and the lie — and enters the Ogdoad naked.

facets.facet_name: The Divine Man Who Fell in Love with Nature
facets.core_claim: Seeing his own beautiful form in the water and shadow of Nature, the Man willed to dwell there; Nature wrapped him in her embrace, and the two became lovers.

facets.facet_name: The First-Born God Who Taught Hermes
facets.core_claim: "I have heard the Good Daimon say — and had he put it in writing he would greatly have benefited the human race — that mind is the soul of God."

facets.facet_name: Serpent Guardian of City and Home
facets.core_claim: As a crowned serpent he guards the city and the storeroom, receiving offerings of wine and bringing abundance.

facets.facet_name: As Below, So Above — the Miracle of the One Thing
facets.core_claim: "That which is below is like that which is above, and that which is above is like that which is below, to accomplish the miracles of the One Thing. And as all things came from the One by the meditation of the One, so all things are born from this One Thing by adaptation."

facets.facet_name: Telesma — Separating the Subtle from the Gross
facets.core_claim: "Separate the earth from the fire, the subtle from the gross, gently and with great skill. It ascends from earth to heaven and descends again to earth, and receives the power of the superior and the inferior."

facets.facet_name: The World Soul and Its Spirit
facets.core_claim: The world-spirit is the medium between the world soul and the world body; the magus, by matching earthly things to it, "marries heaven to earth."

facets.facet_name: Gods Made by Human Art
facets.core_claim: "Humanity, mindful of its nature and origin, persists in imitating divinity: as the Father made the eternal gods like himself, so humanity fashioned its own gods in the likeness of its own features."
facets.scholarly_note: Augustine attacked this passage as proof that pagan statues housed demons.

facets.facet_name: Spirit of Transformation, Beginning and End of the Work
facets.core_claim: "Our Mercurius" dissolves the king and queen, unites them, and carries them through death to the white and red Stone; he is the medium joining every opposite.

facets.facet_name: The Fleeing Slave and Poisonous Dragon
facets.core_claim: Volatile and deceitful, he slips away as quicksilver and must be caught, killed and fixed before he becomes the healing elixir.

facets.facet_name: The Red King Who Dies and Is Wedded
facets.core_claim: In the coniunctio the King and Queen enter the bath, unite, die together in putrefaction, and rise as one glorified body.

facets.facet_name: The White Queen of the Albedo
facets.core_claim: Luna receives the King in the mercurial bath; when the blackened matter turns white, her reign has come.

facets.facet_name: The Crowned Androgyne of the Finished Work
facets.core_claim: Standing winged upon the moon or the dragon, one body with two heads, the Rebis is male and female, fixed and volatile, made one.

facets.facet_name: One Is the All
facets.core_claim: "One is the All, and through it the All, and by it the All, and if it does not contain the All, it is nothing."

facets.facet_name: Intellect, the Realm of the Forms
facets.core_claim: Intellect is all things together, each Form a living mind; it is Kronos, full of his offspring, in Plotinus' reading of the old myth.
facets.scholarly_note: Hadot, Plotinus, or the Simplicity of Vision (1993).

facets.facet_name: Soul of the All, Bridge Between Worlds
facets.core_claim: "Let every soul first consider this: that it made all living things, breathing life into them, and the sun and this great heaven, and that it orders them and drives them round."

facets.facet_name: The Good Craftsman of the Living Cosmos
facets.core_claim: "He was good, and in the good no envy ever arises; free of envy, he wished all things to be as like himself as possible."
facets.scholarly_note: The Gnostic demiurge reworks this figure as ignorant or malicious; in Platonism he is wholly good.

facets.facet_name: The Father Who Snatched Himself Away
facets.core_claim: "The Father snatched himself away and did not enclose his own fire in his intellectual power." He is grasped only "with the flower of the mind."

facets.facet_name: The Cosmic Soul Between the Fathers
facets.core_claim: "About the hollow of her right flank a great stream of the primordially generated Soul gushes forth, ensouling light, fire, aether and the worlds."

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Theurgic Epiphany
facets.core_claim: She comes to the theurgist as formless fire and lightning; her wheel, the strophalos, spun with the right names, draws her presence down.

facets.facet_name: Messengers of the Father's Will
facets.core_claim: "Thought by the Father, they themselves think too, moved by unspeakable counsels" — they carry the Father's will downward and the soul's longing upward.

facets.facet_name: The Gods as Self-Complete Unities
facets.core_claim: "Every god is a self-complete henad, and every self-complete henad is a god"; each gives its character to a whole chain of beings below.

facets.facet_name: Eternity Encircling the Zodiac
facets.core_claim: "The power of God is Aion; the work of Aion is the cosmos" (CH XI.3). He holds the zodiac wheel and the ages turn within him.

facets.facet_name: Aion Born of the Virgin
facets.core_claim: At the Koreion they bring up from the crypt a wooden image marked with stars, carry it round the temple seven times, and cry, "Today at this hour Kore, that is the Virgin, has given birth to Aion."

facets.facet_name: The Name of 365 Days
facets.core_claim: Engraved with IAŌ and Sabaōth on gems, his name protects the wearer; his number is the number of the days of the year.

facets.facet_name: The Great Name of Power
facets.core_claim: "I call upon you, Iaō Sabaōth Adōnai Elōai" — the name of the highest god, which binds and looses every lesser power.

facets.facet_name: The Headless Creator Who Drives Out Daimones
facets.core_claim: "I call upon you, the Headless One, who created earth and heaven, who created night and day, you who created light and darkness; you are Osoronnophris whom no one has ever seen."

facets.facet_name: The Bornless One as Holy Guardian Angel
facets.core_claim: In the reworked rite the magician becomes the god: "I am the headless daimon with my sight in my feet; I am the mighty one who possesses the immortal fire."
facets.scholarly_note: The Golden Dawn "Bornless Ritual" and Crowley's Liber Samekh (1921) recast the exorcism as an invocation of the Holy Guardian Angel.

facets.facet_name: Storm-Lord Who Binds and Compels
facets.core_claim: "I call upon you, the one in the empty air, terrible, invisible, almighty, god of gods, who makes desolate and desolates" — the power behind curse and compulsion.

facets.facet_name: Mistress Below Called by Her Babylonian Name
facets.core_claim: "Hekate Ereschigal, against fear of punishment": with her names and the gesture of the sandal, the initiate passes the avengers unharmed.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Rite of Immortalization
facets.core_claim: "Be gracious to me, O Providence and Fortune, as I write these mysteries handed down... that I alone may ascend into heaven as an inquirer and behold the universe."

facets.facet_name: Radiate Lion-Headed Serpent of Healing
facets.core_claim: Carved on green jasper with the seven-rayed crown and the triple-S sign, Chnoubis soothes the belly of the one who wears him.
facets.scholarly_note: The name derives from an Egyptian decan name; the iconography is shared with Gnostic and Mithraic lion-headed figures.

facets.facet_name: Serpent-Girt Lord of the Heavenly Gates
facets.core_claim: The serpent winds round him six or seven times, the zodiac is carved on his body, and he holds the keys of the heavens.

facets.facet_name: Deus Arimanius, the Dark Power Honoured
facets.core_claim: Some sanctuaries dedicate altars to Deus Arimanius, giving the dark power its due within the mysteries.
facets.scholarly_note: Whether "Arimanius" refers to the lion-headed figure and whether it reflects Zoroastrian Ahriman is debated; "Aion" is a modern label, not attested for him.

facets.facet_name: The Twin Torchbearers of Rising and Setting
facets.core_claim: With torch up and torch down they mark dawn and dusk, spring and autumn, the soul's descent and its return.

facets.facet_name: First King of the East
facets.core_claim: "He maketh thee to go invisible"; he commands sixty-six legions of spirits.

facets.facet_name: Ruler of the Qliphah of Netzach
facets.core_claim: In the Golden Dawn and Crowley's Liber 777, Baal rules A'arab Zaraq, the ravens of dispersion, averse to Netzach.

facets.facet_name: Duke Who Teaches Tongues and Shakes the Earth
facets.core_claim: He makes runaways return, teaches all languages, causes earthquakes and strips men of dignities.

facets.facet_name: Prince Who Finds the Lost
facets.core_claim: He declares things past and to come and discovers all things hidden or lost.

facets.facet_name: President of Hidden Things, Disease and Cure
facets.core_claim: He answers truly of hidden things, causes and cures diseases, gives skill in the mechanical arts, and changes men into other shapes.

facets.facet_name: Marquis of Past and Future, Reconciler of Foes
facets.core_claim: He tells all things past and to come, procures love, and reconciles quarrels between friends and foes.

facets.facet_name: Duke Who Understands Birds and Beasts
facets.core_claim: He gives understanding of the singing of birds and the voices of all creatures, breaks the enchantments that hide treasure, and reconciles friends and rulers.

facets.facet_name: King Who Teaches All Arts and Secret Things
facets.core_claim: He teaches all arts and sciences and secret things, what the earth is, what holds it up in the waters, and what mind is; he gives dignities and binds others to the magician.

facets.facet_name: President of Philosophy and Healing Herbs
facets.core_claim: He teaches moral and natural philosophy, logic and the virtues of all herbs, heals all distempers, and gives good familiars.

facets.facet_name: Terrible King of Love
facets.core_claim: He causes all the love that may be, of men and women, until the magician is satisfied.

facets.facet_name: Marquis of Battles and Festering Wounds
facets.core_claim: He causes great battles and contests and makes wounds made by arrows putrefy.

facets.facet_name: Duke-Knight of Wars to Come
facets.core_claim: He discovers hidden things, knows future wars and how soldiers will meet, and wins the love of lords.

facets.facet_name: King of Hidden Treasure and Divine Answers
facets.core_claim: He knows hidden things, finds treasure, tells past, present and future, answers truly of things divine and of the creation of the world, and brings good familiars.

facets.facet_name: Captain of Manslayers, Teacher of Sciences
facets.core_claim: He teaches all arts and sciences in an instant, is the author of bloodshed and manslaughter, tells past and future, and makes men invisible.

facets.facet_name: Red Duke Who Turns Metal to Gold
facets.core_claim: He answers truly of past, present and future, turns all metals into gold, and gives dignities, but he is a great liar and not to be trusted.

facets.facet_name: Duke Who Tells How the Angels Fell
facets.core_claim: He answers truly of past, present and future, discovers secrets, declares willingly how the spirits fell and the cause of his own fall, and makes men wonderfully learned in the liberal sciences.

facets.facet_name: Grand Duke of the Infernal Triad
facets.core_claim: In the Grimorium Verum and Grand Grimoire, Astaroth is Grand Duke beside Emperor Lucifer and Prince Beelzebuth; the Verum gives him rule over America.

facets.facet_name: King Who Gives the Ring of Virtues
facets.core_claim: He gives the Ring of Virtues; teaches arithmetic, astronomy, geometry and all handicrafts; answers truly; makes invisible; and shows where treasure lies.

facets.facet_name: Ruler of the Qliphah of Tiphareth
facets.core_claim: In Liber 777, Asmodeus rules Thagirion, the disputers, averse to Tiphareth.

facets.facet_name: Earl of Tempests and Love
facets.core_claim: He causes love between man and woman, raises lightning, thunder, blasts and great tempests, and answers truly of secret and divine things.

facets.facet_name: Marquis Who Hopes to Return to the Seventh Throne
facets.core_claim: A strong fighter who answers truly; he told Solomon he hoped after 1,200 years to return to the Seventh Throne.

facets.facet_name: Phoenix-Marquis of Poetry and Sciences
facets.core_claim: He speaks marvellously of all sciences, is a good poet, and hopes after 1,200 years to return to the Seventh Throne.

facets.facet_name: Duke of Winds and Drowning
facets.core_claim: He slays men and drowns them, overthrows ships of war and has power over winds and seas, yet harms none if commanded; he hopes to return to the Seventh Throne after 1,000 years.

facets.facet_name: The Faithful Prince Who Guards Against Temptation
facets.core_claim: He discovers all things past, present and to come, gives dignities and the favour of friends and foes, answers truly of divinity and creation, and is very faithful to the magician, letting no spirit tempt him.

facets.facet_name: The Crowned Lady on the Camel
facets.core_claim: She tells all things past, present and to come, reveals hidden treasure, and procures the love of women young and old.

facets.facet_name: King of Transmutation and Wit
facets.core_claim: He makes men witty, turns wine into water and water into wine, blood into wine, any metal into coin of that metal, and makes fools wise.

facets.facet_name: Marquis of Discord
facets.core_claim: He sows discord, and if the magician is not careful he will slay him and his companions.

facets.facet_name: Leopard-Duke Who Tells of the Fall and Burns Enemies
facets.core_claim: Within the triangle he answers truly of creation, of divinity, and of how he and the other spirits fell; he destroys and burns the magician's enemies and lets no spirit tempt him.

facets.facet_name: King Created Next After Lucifer
facets.core_claim: He distributes senatorships and preferments, wins the favour of friends and foes, and gives excellent familiars, but he must have offerings and will not tell the truth unless constrained by divine power.

facets.facet_name: Many-Faced Duke Who Knows All Thoughts
facets.core_claim: He teaches all arts and sciences, declares secret counsel, knows and can change the thoughts of anyone, causes love, and shows the likeness of any person in a vision.

facets.facet_name: Earl Who Returns Stolen Goods
facets.core_claim: He brings back a thief and the goods stolen, discovers wickedness and underhand dealing, punishes thieves, and finds hidden treasure.

facets.facet_name: King of the Eastern Quarter
facets.core_claim: Asmoday is "the first and choicest under the power of Amaymon"; in Abramelin, Amaymon is one of the eight sub-princes.

facets.facet_name: Prime Minister and Keeper of Treasures
facets.core_claim: Lucifer gave him power over all the wealth and treasures of the world; he appears when the Grand Conjuration is spoken and will make a pact.

facets.facet_name: Ruler of Satariel, the Concealers
facets.core_claim: In Liber 777 Lucifuge rules Satariel, the hiding shell averse to Binah.

facets.facet_name: Emperor of the Infernal Spirits
facets.core_claim: At the head of the hierarchy stands the Emperor Lucifer; through his prime minister Lucifuge Rofocale and his generals all lesser spirits are commanded.

facets.facet_name: Prince of the Infernal Triad
facets.core_claim: Second only to Emperor Lucifer, Prince Beelzebuth commands his own generals and is called with his seal.

facets.facet_name: Princes Sworn to the Adept
facets.core_claim: On the third day after the Angel's appearance the four princes are called, compelled to swear on the sacred names, and made to bind their servitors to the adept.

facets.facet_name: The Angel of Knowledge and Conversation
facets.core_claim: "Your Angel will appear unto you in unequalled beauty" and will teach you the true wisdom; without him no operation is lawful or safe.

facets.facet_name: Olympic Governor of Saturn
facets.core_claim: He turns anything into stone in an instant, teaches alchemy, magic and physic, makes a person invisible, makes the barren fruitful, and gives long life.

facets.facet_name: Olympic Governor of Jupiter
facets.core_claim: He reveals treasures, reconciles the spirits of the air, gives precious stones and familiar spirits, and can prolong life to seven hundred years.

facets.facet_name: Olympic Governor of Mars
facets.core_claim: He governs war and raises those who bear his character to great military honour.

facets.facet_name: Olympic Governor of the Sun
facets.core_claim: He gives six hundred years of perfect health, great wisdom, the best familiars and gold, and teaches perfect medicine.

facets.facet_name: Olympic Governor of Venus
facets.core_claim: He makes a person fair and adorned with beauty, transmutes copper into gold in an instant, and gives faithful spirits.

facets.facet_name: Olympic Governor of Mercury
facets.core_claim: He teaches all arts, gives familiar spirits, and enables the turning of quicksilver into the philosophers' stone.

facets.facet_name: Olympic Governor of the Moon
facets.core_claim: He changes all metals into silver, heals dropsy, gives spirits of the water, and prolongs life to three hundred years.

facets.facet_name: Angel of Saturn
facets.core_claim: Zaphkiel stands before God over the sphere of Saturn and the sephirah Binah, the angel of contemplation and of the understanding of God.

facets.facet_name: Angel of Jupiter
facets.core_claim: Zadkiel, the righteousness of God, governs the sphere of Jupiter and the sephirah Chesed, bringing mercy and abundance.

facets.facet_name: Angel of Mars
facets.core_claim: Camael, who sees God, governs the sphere of Mars and the sephirah Geburah, the angel of severity and of righteous war.

facets.facet_name: Angel of Venus
facets.core_claim: Haniel, the grace of God, governs the sphere of Venus and the sephirah Netzach, the angel of love and harmony.

facets.facet_name: Spirit of the Sun, Number 666
facets.core_claim: Engraved on the solar table of 6 by 6, the numbers of the Sun total 666; Sorath is the spirit of that number, as Nakhiel is its intelligence.

facets.facet_name: Spirit of Mars
facets.core_claim: Called into the triangle, Bartzabel speaks of strife between nations; his number is 325, the sum of the square of Mars.

facets.facet_name: The Child Angel of Dee's Study
facets.core_claim: She hides among Dee's books, speaks of his enemies and friends, and returns grown into a woman to deliver the hardest teachings.

facets.facet_name: Revealer of the Angelic Keys
facets.core_claim: He points to the letters on his table one by one and gives their sense in English: the forty-eight Calls by which the Aethyrs are opened.

facets.facet_name: The Mighty Devil Who Envied Adam
facets.core_claim: "Coronzon (for so is the name of that mighty devil), envying his felicity... began to assail him"; Adam lost the holy tongue in his fall.

facets.facet_name: Hierarchy of the Watchtowers and Aethyrs
facets.core_claim: Each Watchtower is ruled by three secret names of God, a king and six seniors; the angels below them govern the elements, and the governors of the Aethyrs rule the parts of the earth.

facets.facet_name: The Dweller in the Abyss
facets.core_claim: "I am I": the cry of Choronzon is the ego that will not die; he shifts shape endlessly, babbles and tempts, and is defeated only by one who has nothing left for him to seize.

facets.facet_name: The Hidden Masters of the Third Order
facets.core_claim: Mathers declared he had met them, "human but possessed of terrible superhuman powers", and that the Second Order's authority rested on their charter.

facets.facet_name: Gods Who Stand in the Officers
facets.core_claim: The officer builds the image of the god about himself in the astral light and speaks with the god's voice; the hall becomes the Hall of Judgment of the dead.

facets.facet_name: Guardians of the Four Quarters
facets.core_claim: "Before me Raphael, behind me Gabriel, on my right hand Michael, on my left hand Auriel; for about me flames the pentagram, and in the column stands the six-rayed star."

facets.facet_name: The Twin Contending Heads Averse to the Crown
facets.core_claim: Where Kether is unity, Thaumiel is division: the two heads strive forever to unite with the Crown and are cast down.

facets.facet_name: Founder of the Fraternity of the Rose Cross
facets.core_claim: The brothers vow to heal the sick freely, wear the dress of the country, meet yearly at the House of the Holy Spirit, and keep the fraternity secret for a hundred years.

facets.facet_name: Guest at the Chymical Wedding
facets.core_claim: Called at Easter to a royal wedding, he witnesses the beheading and alchemical resurrection of the king and queen and is made a Knight of the Golden Stone.

facets.facet_name: Beings of the Four Elements
facets.core_claim: They are like humans yet without souls; they eat, speak and bear children, and the undine who weds a man gains a soul.

facets.facet_name: The Servant-Spirit of the Pact
facets.core_claim: Bound by the pact, he brings Faustus knowledge, pleasures and journeys through heaven and hell, and at the appointed hour claims his due.
facets.scholarly_note: Goethe's Mephistopheles ("part of that power which eternally wills evil and eternally works good") is a literary development of the chapbook spirit.

facets.facet_name: The Repairer of Fallen Man
facets.core_claim: What the first man lost by his prevarication, the Repairer restores; by uniting with him the soul recovers its rights and its ministry in the universe.

facets.facet_name: The Emanated Man Who Fell into Matter
facets.core_claim: Placed at the centre of creation as the agent of God, Man was more powerful than the fallen spirits; tempted by them, he fell, and his glorious form was exchanged for flesh.

facets.facet_name: The Supreme Being Who Designed the World
facets.core_claim: Every lodge opens and closes in the name of the Great Architect of the Universe, the Volume of the Sacred Law lying open before the brethren.

facets.facet_name: The Master Slain and Raised
facets.core_claim: Faithful unto death, he would not betray the secret; the word was lost with him and substitute secrets were given until it is found again.

facets.facet_name: Husks of the Broken Vessels
facets.core_claim: The evil side has no life of its own; it lives only from the holy sparks it imprisons, and when they are raised it falls away.
facets.scholarly_note: Scholem, Major Trends in Jewish Mysticism (1941), lecture 7.

facets.facet_name: Seductress of the Sons of God
facets.core_claim: From her came the spirits and demons; she still roams at night, joining herself to men in dreams.

facets.facet_name: Ruler of Nahemoth, Shell of Malkuth
facets.core_claim: In Liber 777 Nahema rules the shell averse to Malkuth, the whisperers.

facets.facet_name: Bride of Samael
facets.core_claim: She is a consort of Samael alongside Lilith and Naamah, a power of the Other Side that seduces and destroys.

facets.facet_name: Night-Queen of Destroying Angels
facets.core_claim: "Do not go out alone at night on Wednesday or Sabbath nights, for Agrat bat Mahlat goes forth with eighteen myriads of destroying angels."

facets.facet_name: Prince of Avarice
facets.core_claim: In Binsfeld's classification of the princes of hell, Mammon tempts to avarice as Lucifer to pride and Asmodeus to lust.

facets.facet_name: Prince of Sloth
facets.core_claim: Binsfeld sets Belphegor over acedia, the sloth that turns away from God.

facets.facet_name: Gateway to the Outside
facets.core_claim: Lam is the guardian and gate of the Outside, the trans-Plutonian dimensions. The working is to gaze on the portrait, enter the egg of the head, and pass through Lam into the void beyond.
facets.scholarly_note: The "Lam working" is a later Typhonian and Thelemic practice; Crowley himself left only the portrait and caption.

facets.facet_name: The Way and the One Who Goes
facets.core_claim: "LAM is the Tibetan word for Way or Path, and LAMA is He who Goeth, the specific title of the Gods of Egypt, the Treader of the Path." The number of the name is 71, the number of the book it heads.

facets.facet_name: The Face of the Visitors
facets.core_claim: Lam is an intelligence from beyond the earth whose form foreshadows the large-headed, slit-eyed visitors of the late twentieth century; contact with Lam opens contact with that current.
facets.scholarly_note: The portrait predates the standard "grey" image of 1960s–80s abduction accounts by decades; the identification comes from later Typhonian and ufological writers. Claims that Lam was contacted during Crowley's 1918 Amalantrah Working are later inference, not stated by Crowley. A link to the UFO batch's "greys" record is intentionally not made here.

facets.facet_name: The First God, Lord of the Southern Star
facets.core_claim: Before the sun-gods, Set was worshipped as the star of the south, Sothis-Sirius; the demonized "Satan" is the memory of this first god of the Typhonian current.

facets.facet_name: Primordial Mother of the Seven Stars
facets.core_claim: The Seven Stars circling the pole were her body, the first clock of heaven; the Typhonian tradition is the worship of the Mother and her son before the Father-gods.
facets.scholarly_note: Grant follows 19th-century popular writing on Egyptian origins; in Greek myth Typhon is a male serpent-giant, not a mother goddess.

facets.facet_name: Guardians of the Nightside Tunnels
facets.core_claim: Each tunnel has its sentinel, sigil and number; by vibrating the name and entering the sigil the adept crosses to the reverse of the Tree.

facets.facet_name: The Dreaming Priest Beneath the Sea
facets.core_claim: "That is not dead which can eternal lie, and with strange aeons even death may die."
facets.scholarly_note: Fictional origin: created by H.P. Lovecraft for weird fiction; Lovecraft did not believe in it. Occult use dates from the 1970s.

facets.facet_name: The Blind Idiot God at the Centre of Chaos
facets.core_claim: "That last amorphous blight of nethermost confusion which blasphemes and bubbles at the centre of all infinity."
facets.scholarly_note: Fictional origin: created by H.P. Lovecraft for weird fiction; Lovecraft did not believe in it. Occult use dates from the 1970s.

facets.facet_name: The Crawling Chaos, Messenger of the Outer Gods
facets.core_claim: "And it was then that Nyarlathotep came out of Egypt... swarthy, slender, and sinister, always buying strange instruments of glass and metal."
facets.scholarly_note: Fictional origin: created by H.P. Lovecraft for weird fiction; Lovecraft did not believe in it. Occult use dates from the 1970s.

facets.facet_name: The Black Man of the Witch-Cult
facets.core_claim: In the witch-house he appears as the Black Man who brings the Book of Azathoth and commands the initiate to sign in blood.
facets.scholarly_note: Fictional origin: created by H.P. Lovecraft for weird fiction; Lovecraft did not believe in it. Occult use dates from the 1970s.

facets.facet_name: The Gate, the Key and the Guardian
facets.core_claim: He is coterminous with all time and space; through him the Old Ones broke through once and will break through again.
facets.scholarly_note: Fictional origin: created by H.P. Lovecraft for weird fiction; Lovecraft did not believe in it. Occult use dates from the 1970s.

facets.facet_name: Father of the Deep Ones
facets.core_claim: Those who take the oaths of Dagon will go down at last to dwell in Y'ha-nthlei among wonder and glory forever.
facets.scholarly_note: Fictional origin: created by H.P. Lovecraft for weird fiction; Lovecraft did not believe in it. Occult use dates from the 1970s.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Chaos and Sacred Laughter
facets.core_claim: "I am chaos. I am the substance from which your artists and scientists build rhythms... I have come to tell you that you are free."

facets.facet_name: The Atmospheric I Beyond Belief
facets.core_claim: Kia is the life-force that has no form; "Zos" is the body and mind considered as a whole, and magic is Zos made the instrument of Kia.

facets.facet_name: Baphomet of the Mass of Chaos
facets.core_claim: Called in the Mass of Chaos B, Baphomet is the living force the participants share and feed, worn like a mask for the duration of the rite.

facets.facet_name: The Witch-Messiah Who Taught the Oppressed
facets.core_claim: "When I shall have departed from this world, whenever ye have need of anything, once in the month, and when the moon is full, ye shall assemble in some desert place... and adore the potent spirit of your queen, my mother, great Diana."

facets.facet_name: The First Darkness Who Divided Herself
facets.core_claim: "Diana was the first created before all creation; in her were all things; out of herself, the first darkness, she divided herself; into darkness and light she was divided."

facets.facet_name: Queen of the Witches
facets.core_claim: She teaches the witches their spells and is adored at the full moon with cakes of meal, wine, salt and honey.

facets.facet_name: Brother of Diana, God of Light
facets.core_claim: "Diana greatly loved her brother Lucifer, the god of the Sun and of the Moon, the god of Light, who was so proud of his beauty, and who for his pride was driven from Paradise."

facets.facet_name: Master of the Sabbath
facets.core_claim: Enthroned as a black goat with a candle between his horns, he takes the homage of the assembly, the renunciation of baptism and the kiss.

facets.facet_name: The Black Man Who Meets the Lonely
facets.core_claim: He comes to the poor and grieving in a lonely place as a man in black, offers that they will never want, and puts his mark on them.
