facets.facet_name: Mistress of Witches and Night Rites
facets.core_claim: "Triple Hecate, you who know our undertakings and come to aid the incantations and arts of magicians" — Medea at the crossroads under the full moon.
facets.scholarly_note: The Hecate scenes of Macbeth are widely judged to be later additions, probably by Thomas Middleton.

facets.facet_name: Mistress of the Night-Ride
facets.core_claim: On appointed nights her followers fly out with her over the sleeping lands, serving her as their lady.
facets.scholarly_note: The Canon condemns the belief as illusion; later demonologists turned it into evidence for the witches' flight.

facets.facet_name: Queen Under the Hill
facets.core_claim: Bessie Dunlop's helper Tom Reid was sent by the Queen of Elphame; through him came cures for the sick and knowledge of stolen goods.

facets.facet_name: Imps in Animal Shape
facets.core_claim: Elizabeth Francis received from her grandmother a white spotted cat called Sathan, fed on bread, milk and her blood, which brought her sheep and a husband.

facets.facet_name: Leader of the Night-Ride and Mistress of Spinners
facets.core_claim: In the twelve nights of Yule she goes about, checking the distaffs: the diligent are blessed, the idle find their flax spoiled.

facets.facet_name: Holy Death, Protector of All
facets.core_claim: "Most Holy Death, beloved of my heart, do not abandon me with your protection" — she is impartial, faithful, and comes for all at the hour God sets.

facets.facet_name: The Lady of the Many-Colored Robes
facets.core_claim: White for purity and protection, red for love, gold for money, black for protection against enemies and for vengeance.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Patience and the Good Death
facets.core_claim: Keep his feast on 20 August, never mock him, and he will guard your body and give you a swift and painless end.

facets.facet_name: The Generous Bandit, Angel of the Poor
facets.core_claim: "Malverde, Holy Malverde, I ask that you look on me with mercy"; he gives back to the poor what the powerful took.

facets.facet_name: The Old Grandfather of the Cofradía
facets.core_claim: Each year he moves to a new cofradía house, where petitioners bring him cigars, liquor and money, and his keepers speak for him.

facets.facet_name: The Old Man of Holy Week
facets.core_claim: In Holy Week he is brought out and set up near the church while Christ lies dead; some call him Judas, and after Easter he returns to his house.

facets.facet_name: The Sun Being Who Became the Spirit of the Earth
facets.core_claim: "When the blood flowed from the wounds on Golgotha," the Sun Spirit passed into the earth; the Mystery of Golgotha is the turning-point of all evolution.

facets.facet_name: The Christ-Impulse Between Lucifer and Ahriman
facets.core_claim: The Representative of Humanity stands between Lucifer above and Ahriman below; the Christ-impulse is the free balance between flight from the earth and bondage to it.

facets.facet_name: The Return in the Etheric
facets.core_claim: From the twentieth century onward Christ appears in the etheric world to developing human clairvoyance, not again in a physical body.

facets.facet_name: The Light-Bearer Who Pulls Away from Earth
facets.core_claim: Without Lucifer humanity would have no freedom; with Lucifer alone it would float off into beautiful dreams and lose the earth. He is to be redeemed, not destroyed.

facets.facet_name: The Hardener, Lord of Matter and Cold Intellect
facets.core_claim: He is the spirit of the lie that says there is no spirit; he seeks to make the earth a machine and humanity its cog.

facets.facet_name: Destroyers of the Human I
facets.core_claim: What the Asuras take from the "I" is lost forever; they will act through the coarsest sensuality disguised as the highest truth.
facets.scholarly_note: Steiner borrows the Sanskrit term asura; his Asuras are a new category, not the Vedic or Puranic asuras.

facets.facet_name: Regent of the Age of Michael
facets.core_claim: Michael does not compel; he waits for human beings to bring him spirit-filled thoughts in freedom, and fights the dragon of materialism within each soul.

facets.facet_name: The Lost Divine Wisdom to Be Found Again
facets.core_claim: "We must find again the Isis-Sophia" — not by looking to the old Egyptian Isis but through the Christ, who gives the power to see the wisdom living in the stars.

facets.facet_name: The Seven Form-Giving Creators
facets.core_claim: "Let us make man in our image": it is the Elohim together, a group of creative beings, who speak and form the human being.

facets.facet_name: The Elohim Who Reflects the Sun from the Moon
facets.core_claim: As moonlight is sunlight reflected, so Jahve's law is the Christ's love reflected, until the Sun Being himself arrives.

facets.facet_name: The Sun Demon, Adversary of the Sun Being
facets.core_claim: In 666 he stirred the Academy of Gondishapur, in 1332 the destruction of the Templars, and at 1998 he would rise again through human beings who deny the spirit.

facets.facet_name: The Double at the Threshold
facets.core_claim: "Hitherto you have not seen me, yet I was always with you"; the Guardian forbids entry until the student can bear to see their own unfinished self.

facets.facet_name: The Hidden Adepts Who Guide Evolution
facets.core_claim: Having passed through human evolution, they remain to help it; the Theosophical Society was founded at their direction to restore the ancient Wisdom-Religion.

facets.facet_name: The Light-Bearer of Mind and Freedom
facets.core_claim: "Lucifer is divine and terrestrial Light, the Holy Ghost and Satan at one and the same time"; the serpent of Eden was the giver of wisdom.

basis: Greek Hermes, inventor of writing and speech, is one of the two gods fused in Hermes Trismegistus
Hellenistic Egypt joined him to Thoth as patron of revealed wisdom
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Fowden, The Egyptian Hermes (1986), traces the fusion of Thoth and Hermes in Ptolemaic and Roman Egypt.

basis: Alchemists name Hermes Trismegistus the father of their art and call its spirit Mercurius
The Emerald Tablet, attributed to Hermes, is the founding text of Latin alchemy
Philosophical Mercury takes the Roman god's name via the metal quicksilver (mercurius)
Both are swift, shifty go-betweens who cross every boundary
Both are thieving, shape-shifting tricksters
Both mediate between opposites and between worlds
Mercurius is drawn with the caduceus of two serpents
Both images unite two opposed serpents on one axis
Poimandres reveals the cosmogony to Hermes, who becomes the teacher of humanity
Revelation passes from divine Mind to the human sage
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Poimandres is Hermes' revealer, not Hermes himself.

basis: Both are divine Mind (Nous) just below or identical with the highest source
Both are luminous, generative intellect from which the cosmos proceeds
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Hermetic and Plotinian systems are parallel developments of Middle Platonism; no direct dependence is established.

basis: Both are the luminous source from which Word/Intellect and Soul emanate
Shared function: cosmic-source
Both are good craftsman-gods who frame the planetary heavens
The Hermetic second Mind reworks the Timaeus Demiurge
Both make the seven planetary rulers
The Hermetic craftsman is good and one in substance with the Word; Yaldabaoth is ignorant and arrogant
Gnostic texts recast the Platonic Demiurge as the ignorant creator
Same cosmic role, opposite valence
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Gnostic reversal of the Timaeus is a standard thesis in Gnostic studies; see Pearson, Ancient Gnosticism (2007).

basis: Both systems place seven planetary rulers between soul and God
Their rule is Fate (heimarmenē) over the bodily world
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Hermetic governors are not evil; Gnostic archons are.

basis: Both describe the soul ascending through planetary powers to the divine
Both culminate in rebirth or entry into the Ogdoad
Both are a divine primordial Man in the image of God
Both precede and ground the physical human
A divine First Man descends into the lower realm and is entangled in matter
Humanity contains his light
Divine Man emanated in glory falls into a material body by his own will
His recovery is the goal of the soul
Both are personal protective daimones attached to a person or household
Later occultists read the agathos daimon as the guardian angel
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Structural only; Abramelin does not name the Agathos Daimon.

basis: The Emerald Tablet is the source of the formula "as above, so below"
Both describe the single principle linking above and below
Both are the One from which and into which all things transform
Both are the alchemical prima materia and goal
The Tablet names the Sun as father of the One Thing
Alchemists build the King Sol figure on this line
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Partial: Sol is one parent of the Thing, not the Thing itself.

basis: Ficino translated Plotinus and built his world-soul magic on the Enneads
Both make the World Soul the bond between intelligible and sensible
primary_text_evidence: Ficino, De vita III (1489), commentary on Enneads IV.3

basis: Both are the feminine/cosmic soul mediating creator and creation
Shared function: world-soul, mediator
Both bring a god to dwell in a prepared form (statue / officer)
Both use sound, substance and image to house divine presence
Alchemical Sol borrows the solar god's kingship and gold
Both are the Sun as ruler
Alchemical Luna is the Moon personified as queen
Both rule the night and silver light
Both are androgynous union-of-opposites figures
Lévi's Baphomet draws on alchemical "solve et coagula" imagery
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Lévi's 1856 figure is explicitly alchemical; the link is iconographic and doctrinal.

basis: The Rebis is born from the conjunction of Sol and Luna
The woodcut sequence shows the king and queen merging into the androgyne
The Rebis is born from the conjunction of Sol and Luna
Attested in: Rosarium Philosophorum (1550)
Both are serpentine images of self-renewing time
Both enclose the cosmos
Aion is shown encircled by the zodiac or serpent; the Ouroboros encircles the All
Both are eternity as a closed circle
Intellect is the first emanation from the One in Plotinus' own system
Attested in: Enneads V.1.6–7
Both are the World Soul bridging creator and creation
Shared function: world-soul, mediator
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Orthodox sophiology borrows Platonic world-soul language.

basis: Both are a rational designer-god who frames the cosmos by measure
Masonic "Architect" language echoes the craftsman image
parallels.scholarly_caveat: No documented transmission is claimed.

basis: Both are the transcendent first principle beyond intellect
Later Neoplatonists (Porphyry, Proclus) read the Chaldean Father through Plotinus' One
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Oracles predate Plotinus; Neoplatonists harmonized them afterwards.

basis: Both are the hidden Father beyond all, grasped only by a higher faculty
Shared function: unmanifest-source, beyond-being
Proclus identifies the Chaldean Hecate with the source of the World Soul
Both stand between the intelligible and the sensible
The Chaldean Hecate is the Greek goddess of magic raised to cosmic rank
Both are mistresses of magic and thresholds
primary_text_evidence: Proclus, Hymn to Hecate and Janus

basis: Both are a feminine cosmic soul between the highest God and the world
Shared function: world-soul, mediator
Ficino and Renaissance Platonists drew on the Oracles (in Psellus' and Plethon's versions) for the world-soul
Shared function: world-soul, mediator
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Indirect transmission through Byzantine editions.

basis: The iynx wheel was a love-magic tool of Hecate's cult
In the Oracles the iynges are drawn by Hecate's strophalos
Both are ranks of messengers carrying the divine will through ordered worlds
Roles compared: "Messengers of the Father's Will" and "Hierarchy of the Watchtowers and Aethyrs"
Both are a plurality of divine powers proceeding directly from an unknowable One
Shared function: divine-council, first-emanation
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Scholem notes Neoplatonic influence on early Kabbalah; no direct Proclus-to-Sefirot borrowing is established.

basis: Same name and number 365 in magical papyri and in Basilidean Gnosticism
Both rule the year or the 365 heavens
IAŌ is the Greek transcription of the short form of YHWH
Jewish divine names entered the magical papyri as names of power
Both names are engraved together on the same amulets
Both serve as supreme names of power
The rite names the Headless One "Osoronnophris", Osiris-Wennefer
Osiris was the beheaded/dismembered god
Crowley recast the Headless One rite as the invocation of the Holy Guardian Angel
Both rites culminate in union with one's higher angel
parallels.syncretic_source: Aleister Crowley, Liber Samekh (1921), following the Golden Dawn "Bornless Ritual"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The original PGM rite is an exorcism, not an angel invocation.

basis: Crowley used the Bornless rite to seek his Holy Guardian Angel, whom he identified with Aiwass
Identification made by: Aleister Crowley, Liber Samekh (1921)
parallels.syncretic_source: Aleister Crowley, Liber Samekh (1921)

basis: Greek-speaking Egypt identified Seth with Typhon
Both are storm-lords of the desert and disorder
The papyri call the same god Typhon and Seth
Both are chaos-giants opposed to the order of the gods
The papyri invoke Hekate under the name Ereschigal
Same goddess of night, magic and the underworld
The magical name Ereschigal is the Sumero-Akkadian underworld queen Ereshkigal
Both are queens of the dead
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The name survived as a word of power; there was no continuous Mesopotamian cult in Roman Egypt.

basis: The rite names its god Helios Mithras
Both link Mithras with the Sun and soul-ascent
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Whether the "Mithras Liturgy" reflects Roman Mithraic practice is disputed.

basis: The papyrus god is Helios fused with Mithras
He drives the sun's doors and pole
Both are lion-headed serpents
Both are linked with planetary/decan rule
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Some scholars link Gnostic lion-faced Yaldabaoth to the Chnoubis gem type; the valence is opposite.

basis: Lion head combined with serpent
Astral rule (decan / planetary spheres)
Both are serpent-girt or zodiac-bearing figures of cosmic time
Modern scholars label the lion-headed god "Aion"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The label Aion is modern; no inscription calls the lion-headed figure Aion.

basis: Lion head with serpent
Ruler over the planetary spheres
Mithraic dedications to Deus Arimanius use the Latin form of Ahriman
Roles compared: "Deus Arimanius, the Dark Power Honoured" and "The Cosmic Adversary (Dualistic)"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Whether Roman "Arimanius" had anything of the Zoroastrian adversary, or was simply an honoured underworld power, is debated.

basis: They flank Mithras in every tauroctony
Triple solar scheme: rising, midday (Mithras), setting
A divine child born of a virgin on 6 January
Epiphanius records it as a pagan counterpart to Epiphany
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Epiphanius is hostile; the feast's link to Christian Epiphany is debated.

basis: Bael is the demonized form of Canaanite Baal, "lord"
A high god of a rival people becomes a king of demons
Astaroth comes from Ashtaroth, the Hebrew plural of Astarte
The goddess of Sidon (1 Kings 11:5) becomes a male duke of hell
Asmoday is Asmodeus of Tobit and the Testament of Solomon
Both are demon-kings who teach and serve Solomon
Goetic Belial takes the name of the biblical/Qumran prince of darkness
Both are high powers of evil second to the chief adversary
Belial says he was created next after Lucifer
Both are infernal kings
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Same tradition, hierarchical relation rather than equivalence.

basis: Grimoire Beelzebuth is the New Testament Beelzebul, prince of demons
Attested in: Matthew 12:24; Grimorium Verum
The grimoire emperor is the fallen angel Lucifer of Christian tradition, made head of a commandable hierarchy
Attested in: Isaiah 14:12 (Vulgate "Lucifer"); Grimorium Verum
Members of the same infernal triad of the Grimorium Verum
Shared function: infernal-hierarchy, demon-ruler
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Hierarchical companions, not equivalents.

basis: Lucifuge is Lucifer's prime minister and executor in the Grand Grimoire
Shared function: pact-maker, infernal-hierarchy
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Hierarchical relation.

basis: Both are the servant-spirit with whom the written pact is made
Both deliver wealth and service in exchange for the soul
Both are demon-kings who teach all arts and sciences
Shared function: wisdom-bringer
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Shared function only.

basis: Paimon appears among the Abramelin sub-princes serving the four superior princes
Roles compared: "King Who Teaches All Arts and Secret Things" and "Princes Sworn to the Adept"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Hierarchical relation across grimoires.

basis: Both are kings ruling the East in different grimoire schemes
Shared function: demon-king
Amaymon is one of the eight Abramelin sub-princes under the four princes
Shared function: infernal-hierarchy
The goetic name Amon matches the Egyptian god Amun (Greek Ammon)
Roles compared: "Marquis of Past and Future, Reconciler of Foes" and "The Hidden God Made Manifest as the Sun"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Derivation of the demon from Amun is plausible but undocumented; the functions do not match.

basis: Berith is usually derived from Baal-berith, the "Lord of the Covenant" worshipped at Shechem
Roles compared: "Red Duke Who Turns Metal to Gold" and "The Storm-God / Rider of Clouds"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Baal-berith is a local Baal; the link to Baal Hadad specifically is general, not documented.

basis: Both spirits say they hope to return to the Seventh Throne after 1,200 years
Shared function: goetic-spirit, fallen-angel, redemption-hope
Focalor also hopes to return to the Seventh Throne (after 1,000 years)
Shared function: goetic-spirit, redemption-hope
Both spirits declare how the angels fell and the cause of their own fall
Shared function: goetic-spirit, fallen-angel
Fallen angels in the goetic account who keep hope of restoration
Contrast with the irredeemable fall of Christian doctrine
Both goetic presidents heal disease and teach practical knowledge
Shared function: goetic-spirit, healer
Both are goetic rulers who procure love
Shared function: goetic-spirit, love
Both raise thunder, lightning and tempests
Shared function: storm
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Function only; no derivation.

basis: Both find lost and hidden things
Shared function: goetic-spirit, finder-of-lost
Golden Dawn and Liber 777 assign Baal as ruler of one of the ten qliphoth
Attested in: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909)
In the Treatise on the Left Emanation tradition Asmodeus is a king of the Other Side beside Samael
Liber 777 sets him over a qliphah
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The 777 attribution systematizes earlier Kabbalistic demon lore.

basis: Liber 777 makes Lucifuge ruler of Satariel
Attested in: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909)
Thaumiel is the first of the ten qliphoth, averse to Kether
Attested in: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909)
Moloch, the biblical god of child-offering, is named co-ruler of Thaumiel
Attested in: Leviticus 18:21; Crowley, Liber 777 (1909)
Satan is named co-ruler of Thaumiel, the highest of the shells
Attested in: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909)
Both are the shells/shadow side of the Sefirot in Kabbalah
Lurianic doctrine systematizes Zoharic qelippot
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Scholem, Major Trends (1941).

basis: Golden Dawn qliphoth doctrine adapts the Kabbalistic shells into ten averse spheres
Attested in: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The ten named qliphoth are a Christian-occult systematization, not Lurianic.

basis: Zohar pairs Naamah with Lilith as mothers of demons who seduce men at night
Shared function: demoness, feminine-dark
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Same tradition; companions, not identical.

basis: The sons of God went astray after Naamah's beauty, echoing the Watchers' descent to human women
Roles compared: "Seductress of the Sons of God" and "The Fallen Angels (Descenders to Hermon)"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Rabbinic and Zoharic interpretation of Genesis 6.

basis: Liber 777 sets Nahema over the shell of Malkuth
Attested in: Crowley, Liber 777 (1909)
Zohar names Eisheth Zenunim a bride of Samael
Roles compared: "Bride of Samael" and "Lord of the Sitra Achra"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Relation of consort, not identity.

basis: Both are night-demonesses who lead destroyers and threaten the unwary
Shared function: night, feminine-dark
Both are princes in Binsfeld's scheme of seven princes of hell
Shared function: demon-ruler
Belphegor derives from Baal-Peor, a local Baal of Moab
Shows the Baal-to-demon pattern seen in Bael and Beelzebub
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Baal-Peor is a local Baal, not Baal Hadad himself.

basis: Both are the ruling spirit of Saturn in Renaissance planetary magic
Shared function: planetary-deity
Both are the ruling spirit of Jupiter
Shared function: planetary-deity
Both are the ruling spirit of Mars, governing war
Shared function: planetary-deity
Both are planetary spirits of the Sun
Shared function: planetary-spirit
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Och is beneficent; Sorath is a neutral-to-ambivalent planetary spirit.

basis: Both are the ruling spirit of Venus, giver of beauty and love
Shared function: planetary-deity
The Mercury spirit teaches all arts and the philosophers' stone, Hermetic gifts
Roles compared: "Olympic Governor of Mercury" and "The Thrice-Greatest Wisdom-Teacher"
Both are lunar powers that turn metals to silver
Roles compared: "Olympic Governor of the Moon" and "The White Queen of the Albedo"
Seven planetary governors rule the world in turn
Shared function: planetary-deity
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Arbatel's Olympic spirits are a Renaissance scheme; no direct Hermetic borrowing is shown.

basis: Angel and spirit of Mars in the same Agrippan scheme
Roles compared: "Angel of Mars" and "Spirit of Mars"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Agrippa ranks angel, intelligence and spirit separately.

basis: Steiner takes the name and number 666 of the Agrippan solar spirit
Both are tied to the Sun and to 666
primary_text_evidence: Steiner, The Apocalypse of St. John (1908)

basis: Steiner identifies Sorath with the two-horned beast of Revelation 13
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, The Apocalypse of St. John (Nuremberg, 1908)
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, The Apocalypse of St. John (Nuremberg, 1908)

basis: Both are tied to the number 666 of Revelation
Crowley embraces the Beast as prophet; Steiner treats 666 as the Sun Demon
Crowley identified Aiwass as his own Holy Guardian Angel
Thelema makes "knowledge and conversation of the HGA" the central attainment, from Abramelin
parallels.syncretic_source: Aleister Crowley, The Equinox of the Gods (1936) and Liber Samekh (1921)

basis: Belial is one of the four superior princes
Attested in: Book of Abramelin, Book III
Leviathan is one of the four superior princes
Attested in: Book of Abramelin, Book III
Crowley took the name from Dee's diaries and met Choronzon while scrying the Enochian Aethyrs
Both are adversaries guarding sacred knowledge
primary_text_evidence: Crowley, The Vision and the Voice, 10th Aethyr

basis: Both are the dweller/guardian the initiate must face at the threshold
Both embody the unredeemed self
Both tempt Adam and bring about the fall
Shared function: adversary, tempter
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Dee's angels name Coronzon as the tempter of Adam.

basis: Both are angelic intelligences dictating through a medium or scryer
Shared function: revealer, messenger
Both are angels who reveal sacred words to a human seer
Shared function: revealer, messenger
The Golden Dawn joined the Enochian Watchtowers to the four quarters guarded by the archangels
Roles compared: "Hierarchy of the Watchtowers and Aethyrs" and "Guardians of the Four Quarters"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Golden Dawn synthesis.

basis: Uriel was the first angel Dee and Kelley contacted (1582)
Shared function: cosmic-order-maintainer
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Dee's Uriel is presented as the biblical/Enochic archangel.

basis: The Golden Dawn Michael of the South is the archangel of Jewish-Christian tradition
Attested in: Golden Dawn Lesser Ritual of the Pentagram; Daniel 10:13; Revelation 12:7
primary_text_evidence: Golden Dawn Lesser Ritual of the Pentagram

basis: Raphael of the East is the archangel of Tobit
Attested in: Golden Dawn LBRP; Tobit 12:15
Gabriel of the West is the archangel of Daniel and Luke
Attested in: Golden Dawn LBRP; Daniel 8:16
Auriel of the North is Uriel of 1 Enoch
Attested in: Golden Dawn LBRP; 1 Enoch 20
The Hierophant assumes the godform of Osiris, judge of the dead
Identification made by: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, Neophyte ritual (1888)
parallels.syncretic_source: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, Neophyte ritual (1888)

basis: The Hiereus assumes the godform of Horus, avenger
Identification made by: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, Neophyte ritual (1888)
parallels.syncretic_source: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, Neophyte ritual (1888)

basis: The Kerux assumes the godform of Anubis, guide of the hall
Identification made by: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, Neophyte ritual (1888)
parallels.syncretic_source: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, Neophyte ritual (1888)

basis: Both are hidden superhuman adepts who authorize an esoteric order
The Golden Dawn arose in the Theosophical milieu of 1880s London
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Shared concept; the Golden Dawn did not identify its Chiefs with the Mahatmas.

basis: The Golden Dawn's Second Order (R.R. et A.C.) claimed descent from the Rosicrucian brotherhood
The vault of Christian Rosenkreuz is the centre of its Adeptus Minor ritual
Later Theosophy counted Christian Rosenkreuz among the Masters (as an earlier life of the Master Rakoczi)
Identification made by: C.W. Leadbeater and Annie Besant, early 20th c.
parallels.syncretic_source: C.W. Leadbeater and Annie Besant, early 20th c.
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Rosicrucian sources make no such claim.

basis: The Chymical Wedding narrates the alchemical marriage and resurrection of king and queen
Shared function: divine-couple
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Wedding is an alchemical allegory.

basis: The beheaded and revived king of the Chymical Wedding is the alchemical King
Shared function: alchemical-work, divine-couple
Blavatsky's Lucifer as giver of mind and freedom anticipates modern Luciferianism
Both venerate Lucifer as light-bearer
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Influence is general; Luciferian groups cite Blavatsky among others.

basis: Blavatsky reverses the Church's fallen angel into a bringer of mind
Shared function: light-bringer
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Deliberate polemical reversal.

basis: Both bring divine fire/mind to humanity against a jealous god
Shared function: light-bringer
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Blavatsky herself draws the Prometheus comparison in The Secret Doctrine.

basis: Steiner began in Theosophy and edited the journal Luzifer / Lucifer-Gnosis (1903–08)
Both give Lucifer a necessary role in giving humanity mind
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Steiner keeps Lucifer as a tempter to be balanced, unlike Blavatsky.

basis: Steiner's Sun Being is the Christ of the Gospels, the Logos who descended
Both enter the human Jesus and redeem the world
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, Christianity as Mystical Fact (1902) and lectures to 1924

basis: Steiner taught that Zarathustra beheld the Christ as Ahura Mazdao in the sun
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, lectures on the Gospel of St. Luke (1909) and The East in the Light of the West (1909)
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, lectures on the Gospel of St. Luke (1909) and The East in the Light of the West (1909)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Zoroastrianism makes no such identification.

basis: Both are a solar divinity at the head of a cosmic order
Shared function: sun
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Structural only.

basis: Steiner reads the Second Coming as Christ appearing in the etheric, not in a physical body
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, lectures of 1910 on the Etheric Christ
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, lectures of 1910 on the Etheric Christ

basis: Steiner's Lucifer is the biblical light-bearer who fell, re-read as one of two adversaries
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, lectures 1909–1919
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, lectures 1909–1919

basis: Twin adversaries: Lucifer pulls upward into illusion, Ahriman downward into matter
Christ holds the balance between them
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Same tradition; deliberate polar pair.

basis: Steiner takes the name Ahriman from Zoroastrianism for the adversary of materialism
Both are the spirit of darkness and the lie
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, lectures on Lucifer and Ahriman (1909–1919)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Zoroastrian Angra Mainyu is the absolute adversary of Ahura Mazda; Steiner's Ahriman is one of two adversaries with a role in evolution.

basis: Steiner identifies Ahriman with the Satan of the Bible, "the prince of this world"
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, lectures 1909–1919
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, lectures 1909–1919

basis: Steiner equates Goethe's Mephistopheles with Ahriman
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, lectures on Goethe's Faust (1910s)
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, lectures on Goethe's Faust (1910s)

basis: Both use the Persian name Ahriman for the power of darkness bound to matter
Shared function: adversary
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Manichaean texts call the Prince of Darkness Ahriman; Steiner does not cite Mani for this.

basis: Steiner borrows the Sanskrit term asura
Roles compared: "Destroyers of the Human I" and "Mighty Ascetic Asuras"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Steiner's Asuras are a new category; the Indic asuras are not ego-destroying spirits.

basis: Steiner's Michael is the archangel of Revelation 12 who casts down the dragon (in 1879 as Time Spirit)
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, The Fall of the Spirits of Darkness (1917)
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, The Fall of the Spirits of Darkness (1917)

basis: Both are Michael rising as champion at a turning of the ages
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, lectures 1917–1924
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, lectures 1917–1924

basis: Both are divine Wisdom lost or fallen into the cosmos and to be restored
Both are redeemed through Christ
Steiner names the lost divine wisdom Isis-Sophia
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, Dornach lecture of 24 December 1920
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, Dornach lecture of 24 December 1920

basis: Both are Holy Wisdom as a living, feminine divine principle
Roles compared: "The Lost Divine Wisdom to Be Found Again" and "Holy Wisdom — Pre-Existent Divine Principle"
Steiner reads the plural Elohim of Genesis 1 as seven Spirits of Form who create the human being
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, Genesis lectures (Munich, 1910)
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, Genesis lectures (Munich, 1910)

basis: Steiner's Jahve is the God of Israel, read as the moon-Elohim who gave the Law
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, Genesis lectures (1910) and Gospel of St. John lectures (1908)
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, Genesis lectures (1910) and Gospel of St. John lectures (1908)

basis: Jahve is one of the seven Elohim in Steiner's cosmology
Identification made by: Rudolf Steiner, Genesis lectures (1910)
parallels.syncretic_source: Rudolf Steiner, Genesis lectures (1910)

basis: Both stand at the threshold between worlds and test those who would pass
Roles compared: "The Double at the Threshold" and "She Stands at the Three-Way Crossroads"
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Structural only.

basis: Crowley drew and published Lam as the dedication portrait of his 1919 commentary
Lam enters the Thelemic current through Crowley's own hand
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The relationship is authorship and contact, not equivalence.

basis: Grant read both Aiwass and Lam as extraterrestrial or extra-dimensional intelligences contacted by Crowley
Both are non-human messengers of the same trans-Plutonian current
parallels.syncretic_source: Kenneth Grant, Typhonian Trilogies (from The Magical Revival, 1972)
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Crowley never linked Lam and Aiwass; the link is Grant's.

basis: Both are gateways to the Typhonian "Outside" or nightside in Grant's system
